metadata:
Prep time: 30 minutes + overnight soaking for khar
Soaking time: 8-12 hours (for khar preparation)
Cooking time: 25 minutes
Total time: 12 hours 55 minutes
Serves: 1 person
preparation: Making Kola Khar: Sun-dry Bhimkol banana peels completely (2-3 days). Burn dried peels over medium flame until turned to ash. Immediately dip ashes in 1 cup water. Let settle overnight (8-12 hours). Strain through muslin cloth to get clear alkaline liquid (kola khar). Store in glass bottle.
Preparing banana stem: Peel outer tough layers of banana stem. Cut tender inner part into small 1-inch pieces. Crush lightly by hand to release fibers.
cooking: Heat mustard oil in a pan over medium flame (2 minutes).
Add crushed garlic, fry until golden brown (1-2 minutes, medium flame).
Add crushed banana stem pieces, sauté for 2-3 minutes on medium flame.
Add slit green chilies and salt, mix well (30 seconds).
Add 3-4 tbsp kola khar and ¼ cup water. Stir gently.
Cover and simmer on low flame for 10-15 minutes until banana stem is tender.
Expected texture: Soft, slightly fibrous mash with alkaline aroma.
serving:
Serving: Serve hot with steamed rice.
Accompaniments: Plain rice, fried fish, or lentil curry.
tips: Tips: Use only tender inner stem. Don't overcook or it becomes mushy. Kola khar gives distinctive alkaline taste.
safety: Safety: Ensure banana peels are completely dry before burning. Use muslin cloth for straining.

metadata:
Prep time: 15 minutes
Soaking time: None
Cooking time: 10 minutes
Total time: 25 minutes
Serves: 1 person
ingredients: Bhedai lota (skunk vine) leaves: 1 cup, fresh
preparation: Wash skunk vine leaves thoroughly under running water (2-3 times).
Chop onion, garlic, and green chilies finely.
cooking: Heat mustard oil in a pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add chopped garlic, sauté until fragrant (1 minute, medium flame).
Add chopped onion, cook until translucent (2-3 minutes, medium flame).
Add green chilies, mix well (30 seconds).
Add washed bhedai lota leaves, stir for 2 minutes on medium flame.
Add salt and 2-3 tbsp water. Cover and cook on low flame for 5-6 minutes until leaves are tender.
Expected texture: Soft, cooked greens with onion-garlic base.
serving:
Serving: Serve warm as side dish.
Accompaniments: Steamed rice, dal, fish curry.
tips: Tips: Leaves have strong odor when raw; odor disappears after cooking. Use fresh young leaves.
Substitutions: Can substitute with spinach if bhedai lota unavailable.

metadata:
Prep time: 20 minutes
Soaking time: None
Cooking time: 2 hours
Total time: 2 hours 20 minutes
Serves: 1 person
preparation: Clean and wash fish thoroughly under running water.
Crush garlic pods coarsely.
Clean bamboo hollow, ensure one end is naturally closed.
cooking: Mix fish, crushed garlic, salt, green chilies, and mosundari in a bowl.
Stuff mixture into bamboo hollow, leaving 1-inch space at top.
Pour ½ cup water into bamboo.
Close open end tightly with banana leaf, secure with string or toothpick.
Place bamboo in a large vessel filled with water (water should reach ¾ height of bamboo).
Steam on low flame for 2 hours, ensuring water doesn't dry out.
Expected texture: Tender, steamed fish with smoky bamboo aroma.
serving:
Serving: Open bamboo carefully, serve fish hot.
Accompaniments: Steamed rice, lemon wedge.
tips: Tips: Use fresh river fish for best flavor. Ensure bamboo is food-grade and clean.
safety: Safety: Handle hot bamboo carefully. Check water level during steaming.

metadata:
Prep time: 15 minutes
Soaking time: None
Cooking time: 20 minutes
Total time: 35 minutes
Serves: 1 person
ingredients: Doron bon (Leucas aspera) leaves: 1 cup, chopped
preparation: Wash doron bon leaves thoroughly, chop coarsely.
Slice onion, crush garlic.
cooking: Heat mustard oil in a pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add crushed garlic, sauté until golden (1-2 minutes, medium flame).
Add sliced onion, cook until soft (2-3 minutes, medium flame).
Add green chilies and turmeric powder, mix (30 seconds).
Add chopped doron bon leaves, stir for 2 minutes on medium flame.
Add 1 cup water and salt. Bring to boil.
Reduce to low flame, cover and simmer for 12-15 minutes until leaves are tender.
Expected texture: Soft leafy curry with thin gravy.
serving:
Serving: Serve hot.
Accompaniments: Steamed rice, fish curry.
tips: Tips: Use young tender leaves. Don't overcook or leaves become bitter.
Substitutions: Can use thumbai plant leaves if doron bon unavailable.

title: Bajra no Rotlo & Ringan no Oro

metadata:
Prep time: 20 minutes
Soaking time: None
Cooking time: 25 minutes
Total time: 45 minutes
Serves: 1 person
preparation: For rotlo: Mix bajra flour and salt in a bowl.
For oro: Wash brinjals, prick with fork. Roast directly on flame or in oven until charred and soft (15 minutes). Cool, peel skin, mash pulp.
Chop onion, tomato, garlic, green chilies.
cooking: For Rotlo:
Add water gradually to bajra flour, knead into soft dough (3-4 minutes).
Rest dough for 10 minutes covered with damp cloth.
Divide into 1 ball, pat between wet palms into 5-inch circle (6-7mm thick).
Heat tawa on medium-high flame (2 minutes).
Cook rotlo on tawa: 1.5-2 minutes each side until dry with dark spots.
Hold over direct flame 30-40 seconds, rotating until puffed with char spots.
Apply ghee immediately.
For Oro:
Heat peanut oil in pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add crushed garlic, sauté until golden (1-2 minutes, medium flame).
Add chopped onion, cook until translucent (2-3 minutes).
Add green chilies, green garlic, turmeric, red chili powder, cumin-coriander powder. Sauté 1 minute.
Add chopped tomato, cook until soft (3-4 minutes, medium flame).
Add mashed brinjal, salt, mix well.
Cook on low flame for 5-6 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Garnish with coriander leaves.
Expected texture: Rotlo - thick, slightly chewy flatbread; Oro - smooth, smoky mashed brinjal.
serving:
Serving: Serve rotlo hot with oro.
Accompaniments: Garlic chutney, jaggery, green chili, buttermilk.
tips: Tips: Use warm water for softer rotlo. Roast brinjal thoroughly for smoky flavor.
safety: Safety: Handle hot tawa and flame carefully.

metadata:
Prep time: 15 minutes
Soaking time: None
Cooking time: 15 minutes
Total time: 30 minutes
Serves: 1 person
preparation: Wash purslane thoroughly, remove thick stems, chop leaves and tender stems.
Chop onion, crush garlic.
cooking: Heat mustard oil in pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add crushed garlic, sauté until fragrant (1 minute, medium flame).
Add chopped onion, cook until soft (2-3 minutes).
Add green chilies and turmeric powder, mix (30 seconds).
Add chopped purslane, stir for 2 minutes on medium flame.
Add salt and ¼ cup water. Cover and cook on low flame for 8-10 minutes until tender.
Expected texture: Soft, slightly succulent greens.
serving:
Serving: Serve warm.
Accompaniments: Steamed rice, dal, fish curry.
tips: Tips: Use fresh, young purslane. Don't overcook or becomes slimy.

metadata:
Prep time: 20 minutes
Soaking time: 30 minutes
Cooking time: 20 minutes
Total time: 1 hour 10 minutes
Serves: 1 person
ingredients: Chana dal (split Bengal gram): ½ cup
preparation: Wash chana dal thoroughly. Soak in water for 30 minutes. Drain.
Chop green chilies, grate ginger, mince garlic.
cooking: Pressure cook soaked dal with 1 cup water for 3-4 whistles (15 minutes). Cool, mash coarsely.
Heat oil in pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add mustard seeds, let splutter (30 seconds).
Add sesame seeds, sauté until golden (1 minute, medium flame).
Add ginger, garlic, green chilies, sauté until fragrant (1-2 minutes).
Add turmeric powder, mix (30 seconds).
Add mashed dal, salt, sugar, mix well. Cook on low flame for 5-6 minutes, stirring.
Add lemon juice, mix. Remove from heat.
Garnish with sev, coriander leaves, grated coconut.
Expected texture: Crumbly, moist dal mixture with crispy sev topping.
serving:
Serving: Serve at room temperature.
Accompaniments: Chutney, pickle, tea.
tips: Tips: Don't overcook dal or becomes pasty. Add sev just before serving to maintain crispness.
Substitutions: Can use moong dal instead of chana dal.

metadata:
Prep time: 15 minutes
Soaking time: None
Cooking time: 20 minutes
Total time: 35 minutes
Serves: 1 person
preparation: Break wood apple, scoop out pulp, remove seeds.
Chop onion, tomato, crush garlic.
cooking: Heat mustard oil in pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add crushed garlic, sauté until golden (1-2 minutes, medium flame).
Add chopped onion, cook until translucent (2-3 minutes).
Add green chilies, turmeric, red chili powder, cumin powder, sauté 1 minute.
Add chopped tomato, cook until soft (3-4 minutes, medium flame).
Add wood apple pulp, salt, sugar, mix well.
Add 1 cup water, bring to boil.
Reduce to low flame, simmer for 10-12 minutes until pulp is soft and gravy thickens.
Garnish with coriander leaves.
Expected texture: Soft pulp in thick, tangy-sweet gravy.
serving:
Serving: Serve hot.
Accompaniments: Steamed rice, roti, dal.
tips: Tips: Adjust sugar based on wood apple's natural tartness. Remove seeds completely.

metadata:
Prep time: 30 minutes
Soaking time: 4-6 hours
Cooking time: 25 minutes
Total time: 6 hours 55 minutes
Serves: 1 person
ingredients: Banana leaf or idli mold: for steaming
preparation: Remove jackfruit pulp, discard seeds and fibers. Mash pulp coarsely.
Mix rice flour with jackfruit pulp, jaggery, cardamom powder.
Add water gradually to make thick batter (consistency of idli batter).
cooking: Grease idli mold or banana leaf cups with ghee.
Pour batter into molds, filling ¾ full.
Steam in steamer or pressure cooker (without whistle) for 15-20 minutes on medium flame.
Check doneness with toothpick - should come out clean.
Cool slightly, remove from molds.
Expected texture: Soft, spongy, sweet jackfruit dumplings.
serving:
Serving: Serve warm or at room temperature.
Accompaniments: Coconut chutney, ghee.
tips: Tips: Use ripe jackfruit for natural sweetness. Don't overfill molds.
safety: Safety: Handle hot steamer carefully.

metadata:
Prep time: 15 minutes
Soaking time: 2-3 hours
Cooking time: 30 minutes
Total time: 3 hours 45 minutes
Serves: 1 person
ingredients: Tamarind: 1 small ball, soaked in 1 cup water
preparation: Wash horse gram, soak in water for 2-3 hours. Drain.
Grind soaked horse gram coarsely with onion, green chilies, ginger, salt (minimal water).
Extract tamarind juice from soaked tamarind, strain.
cooking: For Kattu:
Wet hands, shape horse gram paste into small lemon-sized balls.
Steam in steamer for 15-20 minutes on medium flame until cooked.
Expected texture: Firm, cooked dumplings.
For Saaru:
Heat oil in pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add mustard seeds, let splutter (30 seconds).
Add curry leaves, crushed garlic, sauté until fragrant (1 minute).
Add chopped tomato, green chilies, cook until soft (3-4 minutes, medium flame).
Add tamarind extract, rasam powder, turmeric, salt.
Bring to boil, reduce to low flame, simmer for 10-12 minutes.
Add steamed horse gram balls, simmer 2-3 minutes.
Garnish with coriander leaves.
serving:
Serving: Serve hot saaru with kattu.
Accompaniments: Steamed rice, pickle.
tips: Tips: Soak horse gram thoroughly for easier grinding. Don't overcook dumplings or they break.

metadata:
Prep time: 10 minutes
Soaking time: None
Cooking time: 10 minutes
Total time: 20 minutes
Serves: 1 person
preparation: Wash sesame leaves thoroughly, chop coarsely.
Grate coconut, peel garlic.
cooking: Heat ½ tsp oil in pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add sesame leaves, green chilies, sauté for 2-3 minutes until wilted.
Cool slightly, grind with coconut, garlic, tamarind, salt to smooth paste (add minimal water).
Heat remaining ½ tsp oil in small pan (1 minute).
Add mustard seeds, let splutter (30 seconds).
Add curry leaves, pour over chutney.
Expected texture: Smooth, green chutney with tempering.
serving:
Serving: Serve fresh.
Accompaniments: Roti, rice, idli, dosa.
tips: Tips: Use fresh young sesame leaves. Adjust chilies to taste.

metadata:
Prep time: 10 minutes
Soaking time: None
Cooking time: 5 minutes
Total time: 15 minutes
Serves: 1 person
ingredients: Brahmi leaves (or curry leaves): ½ cup
preparation: Wash brahmi leaves thoroughly.
Grate coconut, whisk yogurt.
cooking: Grind brahmi leaves, coconut, green chilies, cumin seeds to smooth paste with minimal water.
Mix with whisked yogurt, add salt.
Heat oil in small pan (1 minute).
Add mustard seeds, let splutter (30 seconds), pour over tambuli.
Expected texture: Smooth, creamy, cooling yogurt-based chutney.
serving:
Serving: Serve chilled or at room temperature.
Accompaniments: Hot rice, ghee, pickle.
tips: Tips: Use fresh brahmi or curry leaves. Keep refrigerated.

metadata:
Prep time: 15 minutes
Soaking time: 4-6 hours (for badi) + overnight (for pakhala)
Cooking time: 20 minutes
Total time: 6 hours 35 minutes
Serves: 1 person
preparation: For pakhala: Take leftover cooked rice, soak in 2 cups water overnight (8-12 hours) at room temperature.
For badi: Sun-dry urad dal paste dumplings for 2-3 days until completely dry.
cooking: For Pakhala:
Drain excess water from soaked rice (retain some water for consistency).
Add salt, mix gently.
Expected texture: Soft, fermented, slightly watery rice.
For Badi Chura:
Break dried badi into small pieces.
Heat mustard oil in pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add crushed garlic, sauté until golden (1-2 minutes).
Add chopped onion, cook until translucent (2-3 minutes).
Add green chilies, turmeric, red chili powder, sauté 1 minute.
Add badi pieces, salt, mix well.
Add ¼ cup water, cover and cook on low flame for 8-10 minutes until badi is soft.
Mash lightly with spoon.
Garnish with coriander leaves.
serving:
Serving: Serve pakhala with badi chura.
Accompaniments: Fried vegetables, pickle, roasted cumin powder.
tips: Tips: Use day-old rice for pakhala. Sun-dry badi thoroughly for longer shelf life.
safety: Safety: Don't ferment pakhala in hot weather for more than 12 hours.

metadata:
Prep time: 10 minutes
Soaking time: 1-2 days (fermentation)
Cooking time: 10 minutes
Total time: 2 days 20 minutes
Serves: 1 person
preparation: Take leftover cooked rice.
cooking: Mix rice with 3 cups water in a container.
Cover loosely, keep at room temperature for 1-2 days to ferment slightly.
After fermentation, strain if desired (or keep as is).
Heat oil in pan (1 minute).
Add mustard seeds, let splutter (30 seconds).
Add ginger, green chilies, curry leaves, sauté 1 minute.
Add fermented rice water, salt, bring to boil.
Simmer on low flame for 5-6 minutes.
Expected texture: Thin, slightly sour, probiotic rice water.
serving:
Serving: Serve warm.
Accompaniments: Fried vegetables, pickle, boiled potato.
tips: Tips: Fermentation time varies with climate. In summer, 1 day is sufficient.
safety: Safety: Discard if smell is off or mold appears.

metadata:
Prep time: 30 minutes
Soaking time: 4-6 hours
Cooking time: 40 minutes
Total time: 7 hours 10 minutes
Serves: 1 person
ingredients: Mixed lentils (moong, chana, toor): ½ cup
preparation: Wash rice, soak for 4-6 hours. Drain, grind to smooth batter with minimal water.
Mix batter with coconut, jaggery, cardamom powder.
Wash lentils, soak for 30 minutes.
Chop vegetables into 1-inch pieces.
cooking: For Chitau Pitha:
Heat griddle or tawa on medium flame (2 minutes).
Pour small ladle of batter, spread into 3-inch circle.
Cook on medium flame for 2-3 minutes each side until golden.
Apply ghee.
Expected texture: Soft, slightly crispy rice pancakes.
For Dalma:
Pressure cook lentils with vegetables, turmeric, salt, 2 cups water for 3-4 whistles (20 minutes).
Extract tamarind juice, strain.
Heat oil in pan (1 minute).
Add mustard seeds, curry leaves, sauté 30 seconds.
Add ginger, green chilies, sauté 1 minute.
Add cooked lentil-vegetable mixture, tamarind extract.
Simmer on low flame for 8-10 minutes until flavors blend.
Expected texture: Soft lentils and vegetables in tangy gravy.
serving:
Serving: Serve pitha with dalma.
Accompaniments: Ghee, pickle, chutney.
tips: Tips: Use fresh coconut for pitha. Don't overcook dalma or vegetables become mushy.

metadata:
Prep time: 20 minutes
Soaking time: 2-3 hours
Cooking time: 35 minutes
Total time: 5 hours 55 minutes
Serves: 1 person
ingredients: Mixed lentils (toor, moong, chana): ½ cup
Vegetables (pumpkin, yam, brinjal, carrot): 1½ cups, chopped
preparation: Wash lentils, soak for 2-3 hours. Drain.
Chop all vegetables into 1-inch pieces.
Extract tamarind juice from soaked tamarind, strain.
cooking: Pressure cook lentils with vegetables, turmeric, salt, 2½ cups water for 4-5 whistles (25 minutes).
Heat oil in pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, let splutter (30 seconds).
Add curry leaves, crushed garlic, sauté until golden (1-2 minutes).
Add ginger, green chilies, red chili powder, sauté 1 minute.
Add cooked lentil-vegetable mixture, tamarind extract.
Simmer on low flame for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Garnish with coriander leaves.
Expected texture: Soft lentils and vegetables in thick, tangy gravy.
serving:
Serving: Serve hot.
Accompaniments: Steamed rice, ghee, pickle.
tips: Tips: Use seasonal vegetables. Adjust tamarind based on desired tanginess.

Soaking time: None
Cooking time: 20 minutes
Total time: 30 minutes
Serves: 1 person
ingredients: Tamarind: 1 small ball, soaked in 1 cup water
preparation: Take leftover cooked rice.
Extract tamarind juice, strain.
cooking: Heat oil in pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add mustard seeds, let splutter (30 seconds).
Add ginger, green chilies, curry leaves, sauté 1 minute.
Add tamarind extract, turmeric, salt, sugar.
Bring to boil, reduce to low flame.
Add cooked rice, mix gently.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes until rice absorbs flavors.

serving:

metadata:
Prep time: 20 minutes
Soaking time: 4-6 hours
Cooking time: 30 minutes
Total time: 7 hours 50 minutes
Serves: 1 person
preparation: Wash horse gram, soak for 4-6 hours. Drain, grind to coarse paste with minimal water.
Mix jowar flour and salt for bhakri.
cooking: For Pithla:
Heat oil in pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add mustard seeds, curry leaves, let splutter (30 seconds).
Add chopped onion, sauté until translucent (2-3 minutes).
Add ginger, garlic, green chilies, sauté 1-2 minutes.
Add turmeric, red chili powder, mix (30 seconds).
Add ground horse gram paste, salt, mix well.
Add 2 cups water gradually, stirring to avoid lumps.
Cook on medium flame for 10-12 minutes, stirring continuously until thick.
Garnish with coriander leaves.
Expected texture: Thick, porridge-like consistency.
For Bhakri:
Add water gradually to jowar flour, knead into soft dough (3-4 minutes).
Divide into 1 ball, pat between wet palms into 5-inch circle.
Heat tawa on medium-high flame (2 minutes).
Cook bhakri on tawa: 2 minutes each side until dry with dark spots.
Hold over direct flame 30-40 seconds until puffed.
Apply ghee.
serving:
Serving: Serve pithla hot with bhakri.
Accompaniments: Onion slices, green chili, pickle.
tips: Tips: Stir pithla continuously to prevent lumps. Use warm water for softer bhakri.

metadata:
Prep time: 15 minutes
Soaking time: None
Cooking time: 20 minutes
Total time: 35 minutes
Serves: 1 person
preparation: Peel raw banana, chop into 1-inch pieces.
Grate coconut, soak tamarind in 2 tbsp warm water.
cooking: Pressure cook banana pieces with turmeric, salt, ½ cup water for 2 whistles (10 minutes). Drain excess water.
Grind coconut, green chilies, cumin, tamarind to smooth paste.
Heat oil in pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add mustard seeds, curry leaves, let splutter (30 seconds).
Add cooked banana, coconut paste, mix well.
Cook on low flame for 5-6 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Expected texture: Tender banana in thick coconut gravy.
serving:
Serving: Serve hot.
Accompaniments: Steamed rice, roti, dal.
tips: Tips: Use raw, green banana (not ripe). Cook banana thoroughly to remove rawness.

metadata:
Prep time: 15 minutes
Soaking time: None
Cooking time: 15 minutes
Total time: 30 minutes
Serves: 1 person (makes ½ cup chutney powder)
preparation: Wash ivy gourd, slice very thin.
Separate chana dal, urad dal.
cooking: Heat oil in pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add chana dal, urad dal, roast until golden (2-3 minutes, medium flame).
Add dried red chilies, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, sesame seeds, roast 2 minutes until aromatic.
Add sliced ivy gourd, garlic, roast on low flame for 8-10 minutes until gourd is completely dry and crisp.
Cool completely.
Grind to coarse powder with salt.
Expected texture: Dry, coarse, spicy chutney powder.
serving:
Serving: Serve as dry chutney.
Accompaniments: Hot rice with ghee, roti, idli, dosa.
tips: Tips: Roast until completely dry for longer shelf life. Store in airtight container.
safety: Safety: Ensure gourd is completely dry before grinding to prevent mold.

metadata:
Prep time: 10 minutes
Soaking time: 1-2 days (fermentation)
Cooking time: 15 minutes
Total time: 2 days 25 minutes
Serves: 1 person
ingredients: Black rice (or regular rice): ½ cup
preparation: Wash rice thoroughly.
cooking: Cook rice with 2 cups water until soft (15 minutes). Cool.
Transfer to container, add 1 cup water, cover loosely.
Keep at room temperature for 1-2 days to ferment.
After fermentation, heat oil in pan (1 minute).
Add mustard seeds, let splutter (30 seconds).
Add ginger, green chilies, curry leaves, sauté 1 minute.
Add fermented rice mixture, salt, bring to boil.
Simmer on low flame for 5-6 minutes.
Expected texture: Thin, slightly sour, probiotic rice porridge.
serving:
Serving: Serve warm.
Accompaniments: Fried vegetables, pickle, boiled egg.
tips: Tips: Fermentation time varies with climate. In summer, 1 day is sufficient.
safety: Safety: Discard if smell is off or mold appears.

metadata:
Prep time: 15 minutes
Soaking time: 2-3 hours
Cooking time: 30 minutes
Total time: 5 hours 45 minutes
Serves: 1 person
preparation: Wash bajra and moong dal separately, soak for 2-3 hours. Drain.
Chop onion, tomato, grate ginger, crush garlic.
cooking: Heat oil in pressure cooker over medium flame (1 minute).
Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, let splutter (30 seconds).
Add chopped onion, sauté until translucent (2-3 minutes).
Add ginger, garlic, green chilies, sauté 1-2 minutes.
Add tomato, turmeric, red chili powder, cook until soft (3-4 minutes).
Add soaked bajra, moong dal, salt, mix well.
Add 3 cups water, pressure cook for 4-5 whistles (20-25 minutes).
Open after pressure settles, mash lightly.
Garnish with coriander leaves.
Expected texture: Soft, porridge-like khichdi.
serving:
Serving: Serve hot.
Accompaniments: Ghee, pickle, yogurt, papad.
tips: Tips: Soak bajra thoroughly for easier cooking. Adjust water for desired consistency.

Cooking time: 20 minutes
Total time: 40 minutes
Serves: 1 person

preparation: Chop onion, green chilies, grate ginger, crush garlic.
cooking: Heat oil in pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add mustard seeds, curry leaves, let splutter (30 seconds).
Add chopped onion, sauté until translucent (2-3 minutes).
Add ginger, garlic, green chilies, sauté 1-2 minutes.
Add turmeric, red chili powder, mix (30 seconds).

Add 1½ cups water gradually, stirring continuously.
Cook on medium flame for 8-10 minutes, stirring continuously until thick.

serving:

metadata:
Prep time: 15 minutes
Soaking time: None
Cooking time: 20 minutes
Total time: 35 minutes
Serves: 1 person
preparation: Wash bamboo shoot, slice very thin.
Extract lemon juice, chop onion, grate ginger, crush garlic.
cooking: Heat oil in pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add mustard seeds, curry leaves, let splutter (30 seconds).
Add chopped onion, sauté until translucent (2-3 minutes).
Add ginger, garlic, green chilies, sauté 1-2 minutes.
Add bamboo shoot, turmeric, salt, mix well.
Add 1 cup water, bring to boil.
Reduce to low flame, cover and simmer for 12-15 minutes until bamboo shoot is tender.
Add lemon juice, mix well.
Garnish with coriander leaves.
Expected texture: Tender bamboo shoot in tangy, light gravy.
serving:
Serving: Serve hot.
Accompaniments: Steamed rice, roti, dal.
tips: Tips: Use fresh bamboo shoot. Soak in water for 30 minutes before cooking to reduce bitterness.

metadata:
Prep time: 20 minutes
Soaking time: None
Cooking time: 25 minutes
Total time: 45 minutes
Serves: 1 person
ingredients: Bamboo shoot: ½ cup, sliced thin
preparation: Wash pork, chop into small pieces.
Wash bamboo shoot, slice thin.
Grate ginger, crush garlic, chop green chilies.
cooking: For Hmarcha Rawt:
Heat oil in pan over medium flame (1 minute).
Add crushed garlic, sauté until golden (1-2 minutes).
Add chopped pork, sauté until browned (5-6 minutes, medium flame).
Add ginger, green chilies, bamboo shoot, salt, mix well.
Add ½ cup water, cover and cook on low flame for 15-18 minutes until pork is tender.
Expected texture: Tender pork with bamboo shoot in light gravy.
For Sawhchiar:
Wash rice, cook with 1 cup water and salt until soft (15 minutes).
Expected texture: Soft, sticky rice.
serving:
Serving: Serve hmarcha rawt with sawhchiar.
Accompaniments: Green chili, pickle.
tips: Tips: Use fresh pork for best flavor. Cook pork thoroughly.
safety: Safety: Ensure pork is fully cooked before serving.

metadata:
Prep time: 20 minutes
Soaking time: None
Cooking time: 30 minutes
Total time: 50 minutes
Serves: 1 person
preparation: Wash chicken, chop into small pieces.
Wash bamboo shoot, slice thin.
Grate ginger, crush garlic, chop green chilies.

ingredients: Turnip (gogji): 100 g (½ small), peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
preparation: Rinse rajma thoroughly. Soak in 1 cup (250 ml) water for at least 1 hour (or overnight).
Peel turnip, cut into cubes, rinse, and set aside.
Grate ginger; measure spices.
cooking: Cook rajma: Drain soaking water. In a small pressure cooker, add rajma + 1 cup (250 ml) fresh water. Pressure cook on medium flame for 12–15 minutes (about 6–8 whistles on older cookers) until beans are soft. Keep aside.youtube
Sauté turnip: Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil in a small pan on medium flame. Add ¼ tsp cumin seeds; let splutter (~20 seconds).
Add turnip cubes; stir-fry 2 minutes on medium flame.
Add ¼ tsp dry ginger, ⅛ tsp turmeric, ¼ tsp Kashmiri chili, ½ tsp salt. Stir 1 minute.
Add ½ cup (125 ml) water. Cover and simmer on low flame 10–12 minutes until turnip is tender but not mushy.
Combine: Add cooked rajma with its liquid to the turnip. Simmer together on low flame 8–10 minutes. Mash a few beans lightly to thicken gravy.
Finish: Add grated ginger and a pinch of fennel powder. Cook 1 minute more.

Texture: Thick, stew-like; beans soft, turnip tender.
Serve: Hot with 1 small bowl steamed rice or 1 small roti.
Tips: Soak rajma longer for quicker cooking. Substitute navy beans if rajma unavailable.

preparation: Wash greens thoroughly in 2–3 changes of water. Chop roughly.

cooking: Blanch greens: In a small pot, bring 1 cup (250 ml) water to boil on medium flame. Add greens; boil 5 minutes. Drain, squeeze lightly, set aside.
Temper: Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil in a pan on medium. Add ¼ tsp cumin; let splutter.
Add garlic slices; fry 1 minute until golden.
Add blanched greens; stir-fry 2 minutes.
Add ¼ tsp dry ginger, ⅛ tsp turmeric, ¼ tsp chili powder, ½ tsp salt. Stir 1 minute.
Add ½ cup (125 ml) water. Simmer covered on low flame 10–12 minutes.
Thicken (optional): Mix ½ tsp rice flour with 1 tbsp water; stir into saag. Cook 2 minutes more.

Texture: Soft, slightly thick gravy.
Serve: With steamed rice or 1 small makki/bajra roti.
Tips: Substitute spinach + mustard greens if dandelion unavailable.

metadata: A warm, iron-rich porridge made from fresh ragi “milk.”
ingredients: Finger millet (ragi/panja pullu), whole grains: 2 tbsp (about 20 g)

cooking: Total active time: ~20 minutes (excluding soak)
serving: Serving

safety: Safety: Stir constantly to prevent sticking/burning; ensure it’s lukewarm before eating.
